rationale: Implementation correctly refuses disallowed models with proper exception infrastructure and passes 33 tests. However, three actionable findings prevent approval: (1) semantic misuse of ModelNotAllowedException conflates distinct error types ('model not found' vs 'not allowed'), making error handling ambiguous for callers; (2) five edge cases identified (empty model_name, None project.id, whitespace, distinguish allow-list empty vs. model-not-in-list) that could produce misleading error messages or fail silently; (3) Acceptance Criterion 3 (default model fallback when default is excluded by project narrowing) is not implemented. All findings are addressable in a focused fix-up round.

business_review.criterion: Negative case: request naming a disallowed model is refused (not substituted)
business_review.notes: get_model_details() raises ModelNotAllowedException when model is disallowed; no silent substitution.

business_review.criterion: Message names both model and project in the error
business_review.notes: Exception message includes both model name and project ID when project context is present.

business_review.criterion: Default selection: when platform default is excluded, an allowed model is used instead
business_review.notes: No implementation or test for fallback when configured default is excluded by project narrowing. Acceptance criterion unaddressed.

business_review.criterion: Project isolation: removing a model from one project's set must not affect others
business_review.notes: Project-level filtering is independent; integration test confirms cross-project isolation.

business_review.criterion: Consistency: CLI/web/API all see same filtered models
business_review.notes: All paths use same _filter_models_by_project() method; integration test confirms consistency.

business_review.criterion: Backward compatibility: call sites without project context still work
business_review.notes: Optional project parameter defaults to None; all models visible when project is absent.

standards_review.notes: ModelNotAllowedException docstring specifies 'not allowed for project' but is raised for both 'model not found' and 'not allowed'. Semantic confusion.
Edge case handling gaps: empty model_name, None project.id when project exists, ambiguous messages for deny-all allow-list.
model_name with leading/trailing whitespace silently fails to match; no explicit validation or normalization.

findings.problem: Semantic misuse of ModelNotAllowedException for two distinct error cases
findings.impact: Exception is raised for both 'model not found' (line 145-149) and 'model not allowed for project' (line 157-161), but docstring specifies only the latter. Callers cannot distinguish genuine access violations from missing models, reducing error clarity.
findings.recommendation: Create separate NotFoundException for missing models, or extend ModelNotAllowedException to list both cases and adjust error messages accordingly.

findings.problem: Exception omits project context when project object exists but project.id is None
findings.impact: When project exists but project.id is None (e.g., unsaved Application), exception message breaks acceptance criterion 2 (message names both model and project).
findings.recommendation: Require project.id to be non-None or handle None explicitly in exception construction.

findings.problem: Exception details don't distinguish 'model not found' from 'explicitly denied by allow-list'
findings.impact: When allowed_models=[] (deny-all), user message is semantically incorrect for that case.
findings.recommendation: Pass explicit differentiated messages from caller instead of generic fallback.

findings.problem: model_name with leading/trailing whitespace silently produces 'not found' error
findings.impact: model_name=' gpt-4' fails to match and raises misleading error with no signal that whitespace is the issue.
findings.recommendation: Normalize model_name by stripping whitespace before matching.

findings.problem: Acceptance Criterion 3 unimplemented: no default model fallback when platform default is excluded
findings.impact: When project excludes the configured default model, no fallback logic picks a substitute. Clients must guess which model to use.
findings.recommendation: Implement _select_default_model() to pick first allowed model when default is excluded; apply in get_allowed_chat_models().

test_coverage: 33 tests passing (23 service + 6 exception + 4 integration); no regressions. Tests do not cover identified edge cases or Criterion 3.
dismissed_findings: Race condition between check and exception (low-severity; non-concurrent execution model)
Fragile deployment_name reliance (by design; base_name is canonical)
